before_objects.title: Framework-local SI units, the vacuum constants and the exact/measured status of their values
before_objects.statement: Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]. (a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$ carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted (at the adoption of the present SI definition of the ampere, $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ H m$^{-1}$ with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$); the electric constant is defined within the framework by $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$, so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$. (b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the charge density $\rho$ of [[def-em-sources]] carries C m$^{-3}$ and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$ carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] carry T; a force carries the newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$. (c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram (kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ carries kg m s$^{-1}$ ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]); field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$. (d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI, they do not by themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light, which is the physical adoption of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]].
before_objects.strategy: A convention definition: it fixes the coordinate normalisation $x^0=ct$, the unit of each quantity used in this framework, the exact SI defining values of $c$ and $e$ and the measured status of $\mu_0$. The exact values $c=299\,792\,458$ m/s and $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and the statements that the new definition of the ampere fixes $e$ rather than $\mu_0$, that $\mu_0$ must now be determined experimentally, and that $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$ remains exact, are taken from the SI brochure's defining-constants table and its ampere section. The framework's definition of $\varepsilon_0$ by $(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ is a definition consistent with that exact relation; the uncertainty carried by $\varepsilon_0$ is recorded rather than hidden. The dimensional checks of the framework's equations and couplings are developed on the companion examples page of this pair. No numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted and no experiment is claimed.

before_objects.title: Charge parameter, frame charge and current densities, volume charge and flux, and the four-current
before_objects.statement: Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is not asserted. (b) [Smooth source fields] A smooth (volume) source field on $\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the frame charge density (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the frame current density (A m$^{-2}$). For each $t\in I$: the charge of a compact Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$ at time $t$ is $Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)\,dy$, the Riemann integral over a Jordan set ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]); and for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal field $n_S$ the current flux at time $t$ is $\int_S J(y,t)\cdot n_S(y)\,dS$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them. (c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model, and hence the component transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts. This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents. (d) [Density versus scalar multiplier] Suppose in addition that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and equals $\rho_0U$ for a $C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ scalar field $\rho_0$, the scalar multiplier. With the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$ (so $u^0=1$ and $u^i=U^i/U^0$), clause (vii) of the supplier gives $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$; comparing the time component with $j^0=c\rho$ gives $\rho=\rho_0U^0/c$. The frame density $\rho$ and the scalar multiplier $\rho_0$ are distinct objects: they agree exactly when $U^0=1$ (equivalently, where the source is at rest in the chart), and $\rho_0$ is the Lorentz rest density of the source model. The direction $u$ is a normalized chart direction, not assumed unit- or four-velocity normalized; when the spatial coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, it has components $cu^i$. (e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.
before_objects.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. The charge $Q(V,t)$ is the integral of a continuous function over a compact Jordan-measurable set, so it is the Riemann integral of [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]; the flux is the surface integral of [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]. Clause (c) is the explicit model premise that licenses the use of the vector transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$; the supplier itself states that the identification of a physical charge-current with a vector field is a model premise, and this item records it as such. Clause (d) is a direct substitution into the supplier's clause (vii): $j=\rho_0U=\rho_0U^0u=j^0u$, so the supplier's coordinate density is $j^0=c\rho$ in this framework's normalisation, and the displayed relation between $\rho$ and $\rho_0$ follows; the supplier's own warning that the coordinate density and the scalar multiplier differ unless $U^0=1$ is retained. No integration or differentiation of the fields is used beyond the cited definitions, and no conservation law is asserted.

before_objects.title: A smooth compactly supported density and a point charge on a trajectory are different source classes
before_objects.statement: This example is conditional on the definitions [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-fields]] and the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and it uses the Countable Choice assumption AC_omega named below where the published embedding theorem carries it. (a) [Smooth source] Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ be nonnegative with $\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\,dy=1$ (for instance any nonzero nonnegative smooth compactly supported bump divided by its finite nonzero integral), let $q\in\mathbb R$, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set containing $\operatorname{supp}f$. Then $\rho:=qf$ and $J:=0$ is a smooth source field of [[def-em-sources]]: $\rho$ is compactly supported and of class $C^\infty$, hence continuous, and for every compact Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$ containing $\operatorname{supp}f$ the charge is $Q(V,t)=q\int f=q$ at every time $t$, so the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] applies to this source. (b) [Point source] Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $z:I\to\mathbb R^3$ a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $t\mapsto(z(t),t)$ is proper into $\Omega\times I$ ([[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]; properness is automatic when $\Omega\times I$ is the whole ambient domain or when $I=\mathbb R$). For $q\in\mathbb R$, the pairings $\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_I\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$ and $\langle J,\psi\rangle:=q\int_Iz'(t)\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$, for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, are the point-source distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]: they are distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]) satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in the distributional sense. At each fixed time $t$ this model assigns the charge $q\cdot\mathbf 1_{z(t)\in V}$ to a Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$, and its instantaneous spatial density is the evaluation functional $q\delta_{z(t)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), $\varphi\mapsto q\,\varphi(z(t))$; a source field of the smooth branch instead gives the integrals $\varphi\mapsto\int_\Omega\rho(y,t)\varphi(y)\,dy$ of its continuous density. (c) [The two classes differ] Fix $t\in I$, put $z_0:=z(t)\in\Omega$ and suppose $q\ne0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice AC_omega only as it is carried by [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] in the argument below, through the injectivity of the regular-distribution map ([[def-countable-choice]]). Then no locally integrable $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ represents the point charge: there is no such $\rho$ whose regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]) satisfies $\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=q\,\varphi(z_0)$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. Indeed, if $\rho$ did, then on the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$ every test vanishes at $z_0$, so the regular distribution of the restriction of $\rho$ is zero, and injectivity gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere there ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); since $\{z_0\}$ is Lebesgue-null ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]) and a union of two null sets is null ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]), $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. The regular distribution depends only on the almost-everywhere class, so $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=0$ for a cutoff $\varphi_0\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$ ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]), while the assumed identity gives $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$: a contradiction. Hence the point source is not a source field of the smooth branch of [[def-em-sources]] (whose densities are continuous functions), and the smooth-branch equations are not applied to it pointwise; the point source enters the framework only through its distributional pairings. (d) [Conclusion] The two source classes carry the same parameter $q$ and the same total charge $q$ (the smooth density integrates to $q$; the point model assigns charge $q$ to regions containing the particle), but they are different mathematical objects with different regularity, and they enter the framework through different branches. This example asserts no field value at $z(t)$ and contains no measurement or empirical claim.
before_objects.strategy: Direct computations and one short contradiction. (a) $\rho=qf$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence continuous and bounded; for a compact Jordan-measurable $V$ containing the support, the integral of $\rho$ over $V$ equals $q\int f=q$ by the definition of $f$ and additivity of the integral over the support complement ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). (b) The pairings and the continuity equation are exactly the content of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] under its properness hypothesis; the fixed-time reading $q\delta_{z(t)}$ is the evaluation functional of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]. (c) Suppose $u_\rho=q\delta_{z_0}$ with $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. On the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\setminus\{z_0\})$ one has $u_\rho(\varphi)=q\varphi(z_0)=0$; the injectivity clause of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], which carries AC_omega, gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$. The singleton $\{z_0\}$ is null by [[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]], and the union of the exceptional null set with $\{z_0\}$ is null by finite subadditivity ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]), so $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. By the definition of the regular distribution (which depends only on the almost-everywhere class) $u_\rho=0$, i.e. $u_\rho(\varphi)=0$ for every test. The cutoff lemma supplies $\varphi_0$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$, and the assumed identity gives $u_\rho(\varphi_0)=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$, a contradiction. (d) is the bookkeeping of the two total charges. No field equation is solved, no regularity of the point source is asserted beyond its distributional definition, and the only choice principle used is the Countable Choice carried explicitly by the embedding theorem's injectivity.

For the full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf1_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$
where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is defined through its positive and negative parts ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). This integral is absolutely finite, since $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on $\overline V$ and $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure. On the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption, $Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. The empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal field $n_S$ the current flux at time $t$ is $\int_S J(y,t)\cdot n_S(y)\,dS$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). (c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model, and hence the component transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts. This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents. (d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch] Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a $C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier $\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so $u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic convention is $j^0=c\rho$,
$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$
Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$, including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike $U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is $v^i:=cu^i$.
For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch, $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and
$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$
Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model: in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$ (equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are retained. (e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.

proposed_subjects.title: A smooth compactly supported density and a point charge on a trajectory are different source classes
proposed_subjects.statement: This example is conditional on the definitions [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-fields]] and the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and assumes Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ both for the Lebesgue-volume source branch and for the injectivity of the regular-distribution embedding used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). (a) [Smooth source] Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ be nonnegative with Lebesgue normalization $\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\,d\lambda_3=1$ (the Riemann integral over any compact box containing $\operatorname{supp}f$ has the same value by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]) (for instance any nonzero nonnegative smooth compactly supported bump divided by its finite nonzero integral), let $q\in\mathbb R$, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set containing $\operatorname{supp}f$. Then $\rho:=qf$ and $J:=0$ is a smooth source field of [[def-em-sources]]: $\rho$ is compactly supported and of class $C^\infty$, hence continuous, and for every bounded Lebesgue-measurable $V$ with compact closure inside $\Omega$ and containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, the charge is $Q(V,t)=q\int f=q$; the same value holds for the retained compact Jordan/Riemann branch at every time $t$, so the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] applies to this source. (b) [Point source] Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $z:I\to\mathbb R^3$ a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $t\mapsto(z(t),t)$ is proper into $\Omega\times I$ ([[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]; properness is automatic when $\Omega\times I$ is the whole ambient domain or when $I=\mathbb R$). For $q\in\mathbb R$, the pairings $\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_I\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$ and $\langle J,\psi\rangle:=q\int_Iz'(t)\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$, for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, are the point-source distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]: they are distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]) satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in the distributional sense. At each fixed time $t$ this model assigns the charge $q\cdot\mathbf 1_{z(t)\in V}$ to a Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$, and its instantaneous spatial density is the evaluation functional $q\delta_{z(t)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), $\varphi\mapsto q\,\varphi(z(t))$; a source field of the smooth branch instead gives the integrals $\varphi\mapsto\int_\Omega\rho(y,t)\varphi(y)\,dy$ of its continuous density. (c) [The two classes differ] Fix $t\in I$, put $z_0:=z(t)\in\Omega$ and suppose $q\ne0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice AC_omega only as it is carried by [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] in the argument below, through the injectivity of the regular-distribution map ([[def-countable-choice]]). Then no locally integrable $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ represents the point charge: there is no such $\rho$ whose regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]) satisfies $\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=q\,\varphi(z_0)$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. Indeed, if $\rho$ did, then on the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$ every test vanishes at $z_0$, so the regular distribution of the restriction of $\rho$ is zero, and injectivity gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere there ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); since $\{z_0\}$ is Lebesgue-null ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]) and a union of two null sets is null ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]), $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. The regular distribution depends only on the almost-everywhere class, so $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=0$ for a cutoff $\varphi_0\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$ ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]), while the assumed identity gives $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$: a contradiction. Hence the point source is not a source field of the smooth branch of [[def-em-sources]] (whose densities are continuous functions), and the smooth-branch equations are not applied to it pointwise; the point source enters the framework only through its distributional pairings. (d) [Conclusion] The two source classes carry the same parameter $q$ and the same total charge $q$ (the smooth density integrates to $q$; the point model assigns charge $q$ to regions containing the particle), but they are different mathematical objects with different regularity, and they enter the framework through different branches. This example asserts no field value at $z(t)$ and contains no measurement or empirical claim.
proposed_subjects.strategy: For the smooth-source charge claim in (a), assume the declared Countable Choice. The continuous density $qf$ satisfies both source-volume branches of [[def-em-sources]]. For any admitted bounded Lebesgue-measurable $V$ containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, $f\mathbf1_V=f$ pointwise. Since $f\ge0$ and $\int f=1$, it is integrable, and [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]] gives $Q(V,t)=\int_Vqf=q\int f=q$ through [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] and the positive/negative restrictions of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. For compact Jordan $V$, [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies this value with the Riemann charge. No new convergence or differentiation result is needed. Direct computations and one short contradiction. (a) $\rho=qf$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence continuous and bounded; for a compact Jordan-measurable $V$ containing the support, the integral of $\rho$ over $V$ equals $q\int f=q$ by the definition of $f$ and additivity of the integral over the support complement ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). (b) The pairings and the continuity equation are exactly the content of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] under its properness hypothesis; the fixed-time reading $q\delta_{z(t)}$ is the evaluation functional of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]. (c) Suppose $u_\rho=q\delta_{z_0}$ with $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. On the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\setminus\{z_0\})$ one has $u_\rho(\varphi)=q\varphi(z_0)=0$; the injectivity clause of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], which carries AC_omega, gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$. The singleton $\{z_0\}$ is null by [[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]], and the union of the exceptional null set with $\{z_0\}$ is null by finite subadditivity ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]), so $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. By the definition of the regular distribution (which depends only on the almost-everywhere class) $u_\rho=0$, i.e. $u_\rho(\varphi)=0$ for every test. The cutoff lemma supplies $\varphi_0$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$, and the assumed identity gives $u_\rho(\varphi_0)=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$, a contradiction. (d) is the bookkeeping of the two total charges. No field equation is solved, no regularity of the point source is asserted beyond its distributional definition, and the only choice principle used is Countable Choice, carried explicitly both by the Lebesgue-volume/comparison branch and by the embedding theorem's injectivity.

before_object.statement: Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An electric field of class $C^k$ on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a magnetic field of class $C^k$ is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses: $C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and no regularity beyond it is asserted. Conventions: (a) $E$ is a polar vector and $B$ an axial vector relative to the orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] are proper and orientation preserving, so orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them; (b) the fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at a point of singular source support is asserted; (c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T; (d) the identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and is not presupposed here.

before_object.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework: (i) the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of the mathematical model [[def-em-minkowski-affine-space]], together with the conversion constant $c>0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], is the spacetime of the framework: its points represent idealized physical events, displacements represent idealized spacetime separations, and the causal classification of the model is the framework's causal structure; (ii) the inertial frames and charts of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] are the inertial descriptions of the framework, and changes of description are the proper orthochronous isometries adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; (iii) the ideal clock reading rule along future timelike curves and the identification of ideal vacuum light rays with future null straight lines, both with the same constant $c$, are those adopted in [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; (iv) the laboratory description of fields and sources is the restricted inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the spatial Euclidean structure and the SI conventions of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Status and scope: the mathematical model defines the geometry and its theorems prove geometric facts only; that physical events are described by the model, that ideal clocks read the stated proper time and that ideal vacuum light follows null straight lines are adopted assumptions, not deductions from experiment or from the mathematical axioms. The special-relativity postulates adopted here do not by themselves select the Maxwell equations, a force law or any matter model: the electromagnetic equations and couplings of this framework are further postulates of it. The framework is classical, flat and non-quantum; gravitational curvature, quantum fields and measurement postulates are outside its scope.

before_object.title: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations: smooth and weak branches
before_object.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.

Obligations and conventions: the fields and sources are those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], the operators are the published divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the weak reading uses exactly the regular-distribution embedding, the test space and the distributional derivative named in the statement. The exposition must state that the four equations are adopted, that the choice of the sign and constant conventions is the one fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]], and that no magnetic charge is included; the sources not covered by either branch are excluded explicitly. before_object.title: The Lorentz coupling: external force on a test charge and the continuum force and power densities
before_object.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: (i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where $\Phi$ is the raised-index operator of the field at the event $x(\tau)$, defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. The particle's own field is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no self-force. (ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density $\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model; they describe the local interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed current alone. (iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement $mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
before_object.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.

before_object.title: A smooth compactly supported density and a point charge on a trajectory are different source classes
before_object.statement: This example is conditional on the definitions [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-fields]] and the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and it uses the Countable Choice assumption AC_omega named below where the published embedding theorem carries it. (a) [Smooth source] Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ be nonnegative with $\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\,dy=1$ (for instance any nonzero nonnegative smooth compactly supported bump divided by its finite nonzero integral), let $q\in\mathbb R$, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set containing $\operatorname{supp}f$. Then $\rho:=qf$ and $J:=0$ is a smooth source field of [[def-em-sources]]: $\rho$ is compactly supported and of class $C^\infty$, hence continuous, and for every compact Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$ containing $\operatorname{supp}f$ the charge is $Q(V,t)=q\int f=q$ at every time $t$, so the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] applies to this source. (b) [Point source] Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $z:I\to\mathbb R^3$ a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $t\mapsto(z(t),t)$ is proper into $\Omega\times I$ ([[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]; properness is automatic when $\Omega\times I$ is the whole ambient domain or when $I=\mathbb R$). For $q\in\mathbb R$, the pairings $\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_I\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$ and $\langle J,\psi\rangle:=q\int_Iz'(t)\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$, for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, are the point-source distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]: they are distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]) satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in the distributional sense. At each fixed time $t$ this model assigns the charge $q\cdot\mathbf 1_{z(t)\in V}$ to a Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$, and its instantaneous spatial density is the evaluation functional $q\delta_{z(t)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), $\varphi\mapsto q\,\varphi(z(t))$; a source field of the smooth branch instead gives the integrals $\varphi\mapsto\int_\Omega\rho(y,t)\varphi(y)\,dy$ of its continuous density. (c) [The two classes differ] Fix $t\in I$, put $z_0:=z(t)\in\Omega$ and suppose $q\ne0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice AC_omega only as it is carried by [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] in the argument below, through the injectivity of the regular-distribution map ([[def-countable-choice]]). Then no locally integrable $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ represents the point charge: there is no such $\rho$ whose regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]) satisfies $\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=q\,\varphi(z_0)$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. Indeed, if $\rho$ did, then on the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$ every test vanishes at $z_0$, so the regular distribution of the restriction of $\rho$ is zero, and injectivity gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere there ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); since $\{z_0\}$ is Lebesgue-null ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]) and a union of two null sets is null ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]), $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. The regular distribution depends only on the almost-everywhere class, so $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=0$ for a cutoff $\varphi_0\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$ ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]), while the assumed identity gives $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$: a contradiction. Hence the point source is not a source field of the smooth branch of [[def-em-sources]] (whose densities are continuous functions), and the smooth-branch equations are not applied to it pointwise; the point source enters the framework only through its distributional pairings. (d) [Conclusion] The two source classes carry the same parameter $q$ and the same total charge $q$ (the smooth density integrates to $q$; the point model assigns charge $q$ to regions containing the particle), but they are different mathematical objects with different regularity, and they enter the framework through different branches. This example asserts no field value at $z(t)$ and contains no measurement or empirical claim.
before_object.strategy: Direct computations and one short contradiction. (a) $\rho=qf$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence continuous and bounded; for a compact Jordan-measurable $V$ containing the support, the integral of $\rho$ over $V$ equals $q\int f=q$ by the definition of $f$ and additivity of the integral over the support complement ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). (b) The pairings and the continuity equation are exactly the content of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] under its properness hypothesis; the fixed-time reading $q\delta_{z(t)}$ is the evaluation functional of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]. (c) Suppose $u_\rho=q\delta_{z_0}$ with $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. On the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\setminus\{z_0\})$ one has $u_\rho(\varphi)=q\varphi(z_0)=0$; the injectivity clause of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], which carries AC_omega, gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$. The singleton $\{z_0\}$ is null by [[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]], and the union of the exceptional null set with $\{z_0\}$ is null by finite subadditivity ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]), so $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. By the definition of the regular distribution (which depends only on the almost-everywhere class) $u_\rho=0$, i.e. $u_\rho(\varphi)=0$ for every test. The cutoff lemma supplies $\varphi_0$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$, and the assumed identity gives $u_\rho(\varphi_0)=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$, a contradiction. (d) is the bookkeeping of the two total charges. No field equation is solved, no regularity of the point source is asserted beyond its distributional definition, and the only choice principle used is the Countable Choice carried explicitly by the embedding theorem's injectivity.

proposed_object.title: A smooth compactly supported density and a point charge on a trajectory are different source classes
proposed_object.statement: This example is conditional on the definitions [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-fields]] and the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and assumes Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ both for the Lebesgue-volume source branch and for the injectivity of the regular-distribution embedding used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). (a) [Smooth source] Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ be nonnegative with Lebesgue normalization $\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\,d\lambda_3=1$ (the Riemann integral over any compact box containing $\operatorname{supp}f$ has the same value by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]) (for instance any nonzero nonnegative smooth compactly supported bump divided by its finite nonzero integral), let $q\in\mathbb R$, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set containing $\operatorname{supp}f$. Then $\rho:=qf$ and $J:=0$ is a smooth source field of [[def-em-sources]]: $\rho$ is compactly supported and of class $C^\infty$, hence continuous, and for every bounded Lebesgue-measurable $V$ with compact closure inside $\Omega$ and containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, the charge is $Q(V,t)=q\int f=q$; the same value holds for the retained compact Jordan/Riemann branch at every time $t$, so the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] applies to this source. (b) [Point source] Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $z:I\to\mathbb R^3$ a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $t\mapsto(z(t),t)$ is proper into $\Omega\times I$ ([[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]; properness is automatic when $\Omega\times I$ is the whole ambient domain or when $I=\mathbb R$). For $q\in\mathbb R$, the pairings $\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_I\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$ and $\langle J,\psi\rangle:=q\int_Iz'(t)\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$, for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, are the point-source distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]: they are distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]) satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in the distributional sense. At each fixed time $t$ this model assigns the charge $q\cdot\mathbf 1_{z(t)\in V}$ to a Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$, and its instantaneous spatial density is the evaluation functional $q\delta_{z(t)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), $\varphi\mapsto q\,\varphi(z(t))$; a source field of the smooth branch instead gives the integrals $\varphi\mapsto\int_\Omega\rho(y,t)\varphi(y)\,dy$ of its continuous density. (c) [The two classes differ] Fix $t\in I$, put $z_0:=z(t)\in\Omega$ and suppose $q\ne0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice AC_omega only as it is carried by [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] in the argument below, through the injectivity of the regular-distribution map ([[def-countable-choice]]). Then no locally integrable $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ represents the point charge: there is no such $\rho$ whose regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]) satisfies $\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=q\,\varphi(z_0)$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. Indeed, if $\rho$ did, then on the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$ every test vanishes at $z_0$, so the regular distribution of the restriction of $\rho$ is zero, and injectivity gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere there ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); since $\{z_0\}$ is Lebesgue-null ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]) and a union of two null sets is null ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]), $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. The regular distribution depends only on the almost-everywhere class, so $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=0$ for a cutoff $\varphi_0\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$ ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]), while the assumed identity gives $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$: a contradiction. Hence the point source is not a source field of the smooth branch of [[def-em-sources]] (whose densities are continuous functions), and the smooth-branch equations are not applied to it pointwise; the point source enters the framework only through its distributional pairings. (d) [Conclusion] The two source classes carry the same parameter $q$ and the same total charge $q$ (the smooth density integrates to $q$; the point model assigns charge $q$ to regions containing the particle), but they are different mathematical objects with different regularity, and they enter the framework through different branches. This example asserts no field value at $z(t)$ and contains no measurement or empirical claim.
proposed_object.strategy: For the smooth-source charge claim in (a), assume the declared Countable Choice. The continuous density $qf$ satisfies both source-volume branches of [[def-em-sources]]. For any admitted bounded Lebesgue-measurable $V$ containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, $f\mathbf1_V=f$ pointwise. Since $f\ge0$ and $\int f=1$, it is integrable, and [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]] gives $Q(V,t)=\int_Vqf=q\int f=q$ through [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] and the positive/negative restrictions of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. For compact Jordan $V$, [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies this value with the Riemann charge. No new convergence or differentiation result is needed. Direct computations and one short contradiction. (a) $\rho=qf$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence continuous and bounded; for a compact Jordan-measurable $V$ containing the support, the integral of $\rho$ over $V$ equals $q\int f=q$ by the definition of $f$ and additivity of the integral over the support complement ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). (b) The pairings and the continuity equation are exactly the content of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] under its properness hypothesis; the fixed-time reading $q\delta_{z(t)}$ is the evaluation functional of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]. (c) Suppose $u_\rho=q\delta_{z_0}$ with $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. On the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\setminus\{z_0\})$ one has $u_\rho(\varphi)=q\varphi(z_0)=0$; the injectivity clause of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], which carries AC_omega, gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$. The singleton $\{z_0\}$ is null by [[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]], and the union of the exceptional null set with $\{z_0\}$ is null by finite subadditivity ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]), so $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. By the definition of the regular distribution (which depends only on the almost-everywhere class) $u_\rho=0$, i.e. $u_\rho(\varphi)=0$ for every test. The cutoff lemma supplies $\varphi_0$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$, and the assumed identity gives $u_\rho(\varphi_0)=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$, a contradiction. (d) is the bookkeeping of the two total charges. No field equation is solved, no regularity of the point source is asserted beyond its distributional definition, and the only choice principle used is Countable Choice, carried explicitly both by the Lebesgue-volume/comparison branch and by the embedding theorem's injectivity.

before_object.title: Dimensional check of every Maxwell and Lorentz term in SI units
before_object.statement: This example is conditional on the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the definitions of divergence and curl in [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], the equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]; all equalities below are equalities of units, using $1\ \mathrm{C}=1\ \mathrm{A\,s}$, $1\ \mathrm{V}=1\ \mathrm{J\,C^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{J}=1\ \mathrm{N\,m}$, $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{F}=1\ \mathrm{C\,V^{-1}}$ and $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$. (a) $\operatorname{div}E$ has unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}$ and $\rho/\varepsilon_0$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}/(F\,m^{-1})}=\mathrm{C\,V\,m^{-2}\,C^{-1}}=\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}$, so the two sides of $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ agree. (b) $\operatorname{curl}B$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$; $\mu_0J$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}\cdot A\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$; $c^{-2}\partial_tE$ has unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}\,s^{2}\cdot V\,m^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$, so both source terms of $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ have the unit of $\operatorname{curl}B$. (c) $\operatorname{curl}E$ has unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$ and $\partial_tB$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$, so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ is homogeneous; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ is a homogeneous equation. (d) In the coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], $qE$ has unit $\mathrm{C\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$ and $q\,(r'\times B)$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m\,s^{-1}\,T}=\mathrm{C\,N\,A^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$, so the two force terms add with the unit of a force; and $\rho E+J\times B$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}\,V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, the unit of a force density. (e) The energy density $\tfrac12(\varepsilon_0E^2+B^2/\mu_0)$ has unit $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and the flux $E\times B/\mu_0$ has unit $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, consistent with $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\cdot m\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. (f) The check is exact arithmetic of the adopted units; it is not a measurement, it does not prove the equations, and no numerical value of $\mu_0$ is used or asserted.
before_object.strategy: Direct substitution in the unit table of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: each displayed unit computation is a product and quotient of the base and derived units listed there, with the conversion identities $1\ \mathrm{C}=1\ \mathrm{A\,s}$, $1\ \mathrm{V}=1\ \mathrm{J\,C^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{J}=1\ \mathrm{N\,m}$ and $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$ quoted from the same source. The only structural input is that divergence divides a field unit by a length and curl does the same while preserving the field unit ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); time derivatives divide by a time. All computations are finite and exact, and no empirical premise or measurement is used.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), let $c>0$ be the framework's conversion constant, and let $\delta$ be the Euclidean spatial form of that frame on $n^\perp$, $n:=e_0$, with norm $|\cdot|$ and positive spatial orientation ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]). Fix a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) and a nonempty open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, and put

$$U:=\{p\in A:\ \text{there are }t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\text{ with }x^0(p)=ct,\ (x^1,x^2,x^3)(p)=y\}.$$

Then: (a) [Chart restriction] $x(U)=\{(ct,y):t\in I,\ y\in\Omega\}$ and $\Phi:U\to I\times\Omega$, $\Phi(p):=(x^0(p)/c,(x^1,x^2,x^3)(p))$, is a bijection, because the inertial chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ is a bijection and $c>0$; its components are the laboratory time coordinate $t(p):=x^0(p)/c$ and the laboratory position $r(p):=(x^1(p),x^2(p),x^3(p))$. (b) [Slices and spatial structure] For each $t\in I$ the slice $U_t:=\{p\in U:t(p)=t\}$ is carried bijectively onto $\Omega$ by $r$; the constant vector $n=e_0$ is future unit timelike, and $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the $\delta$-orthonormal positively oriented basis of $n^\perp$ in which the coordinates of $r$ are expressed. (c) [Laboratory fields] A laboratory field of rank $m$ is a map $F:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^m$; it is identified with the map $U\to\mathbb R^m$, $p\mapsto F(r(p),t(p))$, and with the family $(F(\cdot,t))_{t\in I}$ of maps $\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$, its values at fixed time. Such a field is of class $C^k$ when the map $(y,t)\mapsto F(y,t)$ is $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; then $\partial_{y_i}F$ (at fixed $t$) and $\partial_tF$ (at fixed $y$) are the partial derivatives of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. No regularity of a field is asserted beyond the class stated for it. (d) [Conventions] The product decomposition is a coordinate identification inside the single inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$; it is not a Galilean transformation, it does not compare two inertial frames, and it does not assert absolute simultaneity. The objects $I,\Omega,t,r,\delta$ and the identification $\mathbb R^3\cong n^\perp$ belong to the named frame; changes of inertial description are the proper orthochronous maps adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]. The frame is an origin together with an ordered basis; it is not a congruence of observers, and no moving observer field is defined here.

supplier_registry.exact_interface: Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]. (a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$ carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted (the pre-2019 SI fixed the historical nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}:=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ exactly; since the revised SI took effect on 20 May 2019, $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined. The SI brochure quotes the nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}$ as the estimate at the 2019 adoption with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$; this is historical estimate/uncertainty context, not an exact equality for the actual $\mu_0$ or a current measured value); the electric constant is defined within the framework by $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$, so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$. (b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the charge density $\rho$ of [[def-em-sources]] carries C m$^{-3}$ and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$ carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] carry T; a force carries the newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$. (c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram (kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ carries kg m s$^{-1}$ ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]); field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$. (d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI, they do not by themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light, which is the physical adoption of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]].

For a regular patch $(D,\varphi)$, the parametrization induces on its interior the unit normal
$$N_\varphi=\frac{\varphi_u\times\varphi_v}{\|\varphi_u\times\varphi_v\|_2}.$$
The denominator is positive there by regularity and [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]], and the vector is orthogonal to the tangent plane ([[def-tangent-plane-of-a-regular-surface-patch]]). Choosing $N_\varphi$ rather than $-N_\varphi$ is an **orientation**.

For a continuous vector field $F$, the flux in the orientation induced by $\varphi$ is $\int_D(F\circ\varphi)\cdot(\varphi_u\times\varphi_v)$. This is the scalar Riemann integral of a continuous function on $D$ ([[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); replacing the orientation by its negative negates the integrand.

Let $E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be bounded in the metric sense of
[[def-metric-bounded-diameter]] and Jordan measurable, and let
$f:E\to\mathbb R$ be bounded. Choose a nondegenerate rectangle
$Q\supseteq E$, whose existence follows from
[[def-jordan-inner-and-outer-content]], and define the zero extension
$$\widetilde f_Q(x):=\begin{cases}f(x),&x\in E,\\0,&x\in Q\setminus E.\end{cases}$$
The function $f$ is **Riemann integrable over $E$** when $\widetilde f_Q$ is integrable over $Q$, and then
$$\int_Ef:=\int_Q\widetilde f_Q.$$
Independence of the bounding rectangle, for both integrability and value, is proved in [[lem-jordan-set-integral-well-defined]] and recorded as the definition's forward justification. For $f=1$, the zero extension is $1_E$, so [[thm-jordan-content-and-indicator-integrability]] gives $\int_E1=\operatorname{cont}(E)$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

supplier_registry.exact_interface:
Let $f:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable. Its positive and negative parts are
$$f^+:=\max\{f,0\},\qquad f^-:=\max\{-f,0\};$$
they are measurable by
[[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]] and
satisfy $f=f^+-f^-$ and $|f|=f^++f^-$.

The **Lebesgue integral of a real measurable function** is defined whenever at
most one of $\int f^+\,d\mu$ and $\int f^-\,d\mu$ is $+\infty$, in which case
$$\int f\,d\mu:=\int f^+\,d\mu-\int f^-\,d\mu.$$
The function is **integrable** when both integrals are finite, equivalently
when $\int|f|\,d\mu<+\infty$.

For a complex measurable function $h=u+iv$ with
$u=\operatorname{Re}h,\ v=\operatorname{Im}h$
([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]), define $h$ to be
**integrable** when $|h|$ is integrable, and then define
$$\int h\,d\mu:=\int u\,d\mu+i\int v\,d\mu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

1. If $f,g:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ are measurable and $f+g$ is defined
   pointwise, then $f+g$ is measurable.
2. If $c\in\mathbb R$ and $f:X\to\mathbb R$ is measurable, then $cf$ is
   measurable.
3. If $f:X\to\mathbb R$ is measurable, then $f^+=\max\{f,0\}$,
   $f^-=\max\{-f,0\}$, and $|f|=f^++f^-$ are measurable.
4. If $E\in\mathcal A$ and $f:X\to[0,+\infty]$ is measurable, then
   $f\chi_E$ is measurable, where this function equals $f$ on $E$ and $0$
   off $E$ (in particular, $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$ here).
5. If $(f_n)$ is a sequence of measurable functions $X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$,
   then $\inf_n f_n$ is measurable; if moreover $f_n\uparrow f$ pointwise, then
   $f$ is measurable.

For $a\in\Omega$, the **Dirac distribution at $a$** is the complex-linear functional $\delta_a(\varphi)=\varphi(a)$ on $\mathcal D(\Omega)$, with the bilinear convention of [[def-distribution]]. It is continuous: the seminorm $q(\varphi)=|\varphi(a)|$ restricts on each $\mathcal D_K$ to a seminorm bounded by $p_0$ (and is zero if $a\notin K$), so it is one of the admissible seminorms defining the test topology.

Its derivatives are those of [[def-distributional-derivative]]:
$$\langle\partial^\alpha\delta_a,\varphi\rangle=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\partial^\alpha\varphi(a).$$
They are distributions by that definition; on each fixed-support stage the absolute value is at most $p_{|\alpha|}(\varphi)$. If $a\notin K$ all derivatives of the test vanish at $a$, so the bound has zero left side. For $\alpha=0$ this is $\delta_a$; a first derivative evaluates the negative first derivative of the test. No conjugation and no choice are involved. On the empty open set there is no permitted point $a$, rather than a new Dirac distribution. The sharp order of these distributions requires a test witness and is proved in the assigned example later.

Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is not asserted. (b) [Smooth source fields] A smooth (volume) source field on $\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the frame charge density (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the frame current density (A m$^{-2}$). For each fixed $t\in I$ retain the compact Jordan branch: if $V\subseteq\Omega$ is compact and Jordan measurable, define $Q_R(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)dy$ by [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], with integrability supplied by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. For the full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf1_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$
where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is defined through its positive and negative parts ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). This integral is absolutely finite, since $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on $\overline V$ and $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure. On the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption, $Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. The empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal field $n_S$ the current flux at time $t$ is $\int_S J(y,t)\cdot n_S(y)\,dS$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them. (c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model, and hence the component transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts. This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents. (d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch] Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a $C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier $\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so $u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic convention is $j^0=c\rho$,
$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$
Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$, including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike $U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is $v^i:=cu^i$.
For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch, $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and
$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$
Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model: in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$ (equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are retained. (e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.

In a measure space $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ ([[def-measure-space]]), a measurable set $N\in\mathcal A$ is **$\mu$-null** if $\mu(N)=0$.

A property $P(x)$ holds **$\mu$-almost everywhere**, or **for $\mu$-almost every $x$**, if its exceptional set is contained in a measurable $\mu$-null set: there is $N\in\mathcal A$ with $\mu(N)=0$ such that $P(x)$ holds for every $x\in X\setminus N$. Both notions are relative to the named measure $\mu$.

For a test $\varphi$ as in [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], define the **regular functional**

$$\langle u_f,\varphi\rangle=\int_\Omega f(x)\varphi(x)\,dx.$$

This is well-defined since $|\int f\varphi|\le\sup_K|\varphi|\int_K|f|$ for $K=\operatorname{supp}\varphi$. It is complex-linear in $f$ and in $\varphi$ and depends only on the almost-everywhere class of $f$. For an empty support the integral is zero. The subsequent embedding theorem establishes continuity, so that this is a distribution, and injectivity modulo almost-everywhere equality. That theorem states the Countable Choice cost of its injectivity proof; no choice is needed to define the displayed pairing.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, with $n\ge1$. A complex-valued function is smooth if its real and imaginary parts are $C^k$ for every finite $k$, in the sense of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. Coordinate derivatives act on these two parts separately. We write $\partial^\alpha$ for the multi-index convention there, and $\partial^0\varphi=\varphi$.

The **test-function space** is $\mathcal D(\Omega)=C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb C)$: its members are smooth functions whose support, the closure in $\Omega$ of their nonzero set, is a compact subset of $\Omega$. Equivalently, the zero extension to $\mathbb R^n$ is smooth with compact support contained in $\Omega$: compactness gives a neighborhood of every boundary point disjoint from the support, where that extension vanishes. Functions are actual functions, not equivalence classes.

Pointwise addition and scalar multiplication make this a complex vector space; the support of a sum lies in the union of the two compact supports. The zero function has empty support. If $\Omega=\varnothing$ there is just the empty function, which is the zero vector. The topology is specified in subsequent definitions. Distribution pairings throughout this page are complex bilinear, with no conjugation on test functions. One may restrict all constructions to real scalars.

supplier_registry.exact_interface: Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval, $z:I\to\mathbb R^3$ a $C^1$ trajectory, and $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ open containing its graph. Assume the graph map $\gamma:I\to\Omega$, $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$, is proper: the inverse image of every compact subset of $\Omega$ is compact in $I$. For $q\in\mathbb R$ and $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ define $\langle\rho,\psi\rangle=q\int_I\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$ and $\langle J,\psi\rangle=q\int_I z'(t)\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$. These define distributions and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. Properness is automatic if $\Omega=\mathbb R^3\times I$, or if $I=\mathbb R$. Endpoint variant: if $I=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, $z$ extends continuously to $[a,b]$, the absolute improper integral $\int_a^b|z'(t)|\,dt$ is finite, and both endpoint events belong to $\Omega$, the same integrals instead define distributions with $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\delta_{(z(a),a)}-q\delta_{(z(b),b)}$. A finite-history source is source-free only when the endpoint contribution vanishes on the chosen test domain; neither mere graph containment nor test compactness alone supplies this.

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.

Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.

Let $n \ge 1$ and **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]). Every at most countable subset $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$
([[def-countable]]) is Lebesgue measurable with

$$\lambda_n(E) \;=\; 0,$$

so $E$ is a $\lambda_n$-null set ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]).
In particular every singleton is null, and on the real line the set
$\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}$ of rational reals ([[lem-rat-embeds-dense]]) satisfies
$\lambda_1(\mathbb{Q}_{\mathbb{R}}) = 0$.

Let $\mu$ be a measure and let $(E_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ be measurable. Then

$$\mu\left(\bigcup_{k\in\mathbb N}E_k\right)\le\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\mu(E_k).$$

For every $m\in\mathbb N$ one also has

$$\mu\left(\bigcup_{k<m}E_k\right)\le\sum_{k<m}\mu(E_k),$$

including $m=0$, where both sides are $0$.
